S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation) is characterized by developmentally inappropriate levels of motor activity, restlessness, impulsivity, and difficulty inhibiting actions, with relatively fewer prominent inattentive symptoms. Adults may present with chronic inner restlessness, difficulty staying seated, excessive talking, and interrupting others, often leading to occupational, relational, or legal problems. Symptoms typically begin in childhood, but in some individuals they become clinically significant or are first recognized later in life when environmental demands change or compensatory strategies fail. It is distinguished from mood, anxiety, and personality disorders by its early onset, pervasive pattern across settings, and specific profile of hyperactive-impulsive behaviors rather than episodic or situational agitation.

patient.stressor: Marco’s district recently promoted him into a part‑time instructional coach role on top of his classroom duties, which means long committee meetings, formal presentations, and supervising other teachers instead of the more free‑flowing, music‑filled classroom environment he thrives in. As these responsibilities ramped up over the last eight months, his difficulty containing his energy and his habit of jumping into conversations began to strain relationships with colleagues, who started complaining that he dominated discussions and derailed agendas. The combination of complaints from younger teachers, formal feedback from his principal about his conduct in meetings, and his wife’s observation that he seemed "always wound up and talking over everyone" left him worried that his position and reputation were at risk. When his principal gently suggested that what they were seeing might be more than just enthusiasm and recommended he talk to a professional, Marco finally agreed to an evaluation after years of brushing off similar concerns.
patient.chief_complaint: “I keep cutting people off and jumping into their conversations at work, even when I tell myself to stop—I feel like I’m constantly intruding on others.”

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: In every staff meeting I’m bouncing my knee, drumming on the table with my fingers, and twisting my ring so much that people next to me edge their chairs away because I just can’t get my body to settle down, no matter how hard I try to sit still like everyone else.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: During these long coaching meetings, I keep popping up under the excuse of grabbing coffee or making a copy, and I’ll find myself pacing in the back of the room because staying in that chair for more than ten minutes feels almost unbearable, like my skin is crawling.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even at home, when my wife wants to just sit quietly and listen to music or read, I end up humming along, tapping out rhythms on the table, or blurting out thoughts because I can’t seem to just do something calmly and quietly without adding noise or movement.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My wife jokes that I’m like a wind‑up toy, because from the time I get up I’m constantly moving—rearranging things in the house, checking email, pacing while I’m on the phone—and even on Sundays I can’t just sit and watch a game without jumping up to straighten something or start another project.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: In these committee meetings I’ll launch into long explanations or stories from my classroom and just keep going, even when I can see people glancing at the clock or trying to move on, and I only realize afterward that I’ve basically taken over the conversation again.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: Lately I’ll tell myself, “Let them finish, Marco,” but the second someone starts sharing an idea I’m bursting in with my own suggestions, finishing their sentences, or steering the discussion my way, and then I see their faces drop and realize, yet again, that I’ve talked right over them and made them feel stepped on.
